title: Ombudsman warns public officials against soliciting funds for Christmas parties
summary: The Office of the Ombudsman on Friday warned public officials and employees against using their offices to solicit donations for Christmas parties and other unauthorized purposes.

blocks.text: The Office of the Ombudsman on Friday warned public officials and employees against using their offices to solicit donations for Christmas parties and other unauthorized purposes.

The Ombudsman issued the statement following its decision to issue a six-month suspension without pay order against Bayani Galzote Olegario, barangay secretary of Barangay Sta. Cruz, Makati City, over solicitation letters issued using official government letterhead.

The Ombudsman said Olegario issued letters in December 2025 seeking cash or in-kind donations from private individuals for the Christmas party of barangay officials and personnel, making him administratively liable for conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service.

“The Ombudsman found substantial evidence that Olegario's use of his official position, barangay letterhead, and signature to solicit donations tarnished the image and integrity of the barangay government. Using the authority and resources associated with public office to solicit donations for a purpose not established as a government function falls short of the standards of integrity expected of public servants,” the Ombudsman said.

“Such semblance of the imprimatur of public office for a purpose not shown to be a governmental function is inconsistent with the standards of integrity and propriety expected of public employees. It creates the appearance that the government itself is requesting private individuals to provide money or property for the benefit of its personnel,” the Ombudsman added.
Olegario’s conduct, the Ombudsman said, may diminish public confidence in the impartiality and integrity of public service.

“The intended use of the solicitation for a Christmas party did not excuse the conduct, as public officials and employees must not only refrain from corruption and personal enrichment but also avoid invoking the authority of their offices for private or unauthorized purposes,” the Ombudsman said.

If the suspension can no longer be enforced due to separation from service, the penalty shall be converted into a fine equivalent to six months and one day's salary, payable to the Office of the Ombudsman. — RSJ, GMA News
